content:
maya: Heads-up — bringing Neutrino8B (int4) into canary today. initial quant runs looked fine but we saw memory fragmentation on a couple of nodes during spike tests.
ryan: copying logs? which nodes and what pattern of OOMs?
maya: one GPU host (g-ml-12) had repeated small allocations then a single OOM during a heavy 16-conc load. memory graph: steady then tiny oscillations then big drop. attaching short snip: 
```
OOM on g-ml-12: runtime malloc failure at step 4320
allocs: many 32k/64k churn (prefetch + kv writes)
peak vmem: 39.1G, gpu reserved: 41.0G, device free drops to 200MB
```
sasha: sounds like KV churn + small prefetched tensors being freed non-contiguously. did we enable prefetch for the canary?
maya: yes, prefetch=true by default for this model (we thought prefetch helps coldstart).
ryan: prefetch is good for latency but increases fragmentation for int4 kernels because of alignment. we saw this with aether18b earlier. suggestion: try prefetch=false + larger micro-batch to keep allocations contiguous.
maya: quick experiment: ran two runs on g-ml-12
- run A (prefetch=true, max_concurrent=8, max_new_tokens=512): 3/10 runs OOM
- run B (prefetch=false, max_concurrent=4, max_new_tokens=256): 0/10 runs OOM, median p95 latency +12%
elaine: thanks. what about throughput / cost implications? is +12% latency acceptable for canary?
sasha: if canary SLO is p95 < 400ms we'd be ok at +12%. throughput dropped ~20% in run B but resource stability is better. also less KV evictions during long context.
ryan: config diff we tried:
```yaml
model: neutrino-8b-int4
batch:
  max_batch_tokens: 12288
  max_concurrent: 4
prefetch: false
max_new_tokens: 256
kv_eviction_policy: conservative
```
maya: re-ran with kv_eviction_policy conservative and prefetch false; fragmentation reduced, OOMs gone. can we make conservative eviction the canary default?
sasha: +1 to conservative for canary, but we should run a quality regressions sweep (int4 can slightly change tokenization perf). schedule eval set: summaries + instruction-following.
elaine: i'll queue evals — need to capture generation windows and a 500-sample instruction set. also check hallucination rate vs fp16 baseline.
ryan: also noticed the quant kernels allocate a staging tensor per request path when prefetch=true; that contributes small allocations that don't coalesce. for stable long-lived traffic, prefetch=false wins. for bursty user traffic, prefetch helps latency. so maybe make prefetch toggled by route policy (low-latency routes enable prefetch).
maya: good idea — route-level override. default for canary = false, low-latency route overrides to true.
elaine: eval results (first 500 samples):
- fp16 baseline rouge-L: 0.741
- int4 canary default (prefetch=false): 0.733 (-1.1%)
- int4 prefetch=true: 0.735 (-0.8%)
quality diff small but measurable. need to run hallucination regression tests.
sasha: also run with max_new_tokens default 256 vs 512: larger defaults increase mem footprint per session and drive frags. recommend lowering default max_new_tokens to 256 for int4 canaries.
ryan: agree. operational change: set per-model defaults in model-catalog metadata. sample patch: 
```json
{"model":"neutrino-8b-int4","defaults":{"max_new_tokens":256,"prefetch":false,"batch.max_concurrent":4}}
```
maya: i'll file the rollout PR and include load-test results + grafana snapshots.
elaine: once PR lands, i'll run the extended evals (3k samples) and smoke test in us-west1 for 48h.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: canary model image built (sha: a3b9c4f), canary nodes tagged, traffic split 2%.
ryan: one more note — KV compactor interval tweak helped on g-ml-12: bump compactor interval from 30s -> 10s during onboarding (more frequent compaction) removed small-chunk buildup. gotcha: more compaction costs CPU.
sasha: add compactor adjustment to the onboarding playbook with a rollback.
maya: plan: PR -> 48h us-west1 canary -> monitor p95/ooms/evictions -> if stable, promote to dedicated staging.
elaine: ack. i'll post eval links here when complete.
ryan: +:thumbsup:
maya: thanks all — will update thread with final numbers and PR link. :rocket:
